task.title: Delete projects and filter the project list by status
behaviours: DELETE /v1/projects/{projectId} returns 204 with an empty body, after which GET /v1/projects/{projectId} returns 404.
DELETE /v1/projects/{projectId} for an id that does not exist (including a second delete of the same project) returns 404 application/problem+json.
DELETE /v1/projects/{projectId} with a malformed id returns 422 application/problem+json.
GET /v1/projects?status=archived returns only archived projects and GET /v1/projects?status=active only active ones.
GET /v1/projects with a status filter is still cursor-paginated: limit and cursor work as before and following nextCursor visits every matching project exactly once.
GET /v1/projects without status returns projects of every status, as before.
GET /v1/projects with an unknown status value returns 422 application/problem+json.
All existing tests keep passing and the public contract only gains (never loses or narrows) routes and properties.
task.change:
Add two capabilities to the existing Projects API without breaking any current client:

1. DELETE /v1/projects/{projectId} removes a project. It returns 204 with no body,
   and 404 application/problem+json when the project does not exist.
2. GET /v1/projects accepts an optional `status` query parameter (active | archived)
   that returns only projects with that status. The list stays cursor-paginated
   (cursor + limit, response { data, nextCursor }) and the filter is applied before
   paginating, so following nextCursor walks the filtered set.

Existing routes, request schemas and response schemas must keep working exactly as
they do today; both changes are additive.
